# Jacksonville Jaguars at Washington Redskins

**Regular-season Week 2**  
Sunday, September 14, 2014 | 1 p.m. ET | FedExField, Landover, Maryland  
**Final: Jacksonville Jaguars 24, Washington Redskins 7**

## Coach record

| Record | Regular season | Postseason | Overall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This season | 2-0-0 | 0-0 | 2-0-0 |
| With Jaguars | 12-6-0 (.667) | 1-1 | 13-7-0 (.650) |
| NFL head coach, career | 12-6-0 (.667) | 1-1 | 13-7-0 (.650) |
| Against Washington Redskins | 1-0-0 | 0-0 | 1-0-0 |

## 1. Preparation and final game-day decisions

The week began with two defensive backs lost: Mike Harris went to injured reserve and Dwight Lowery to injured reserve designated for return on September 8, the day Alan Ball signed after a physical and Adrian Phillips came up from the practice squad. Monday's walkthrough was the secondary's communication with Alterraun Verner and Brynden Trawick in the first group, before the Washington introduction. Wednesday was the base, protection and run-fit practice with the rush present, Thursday the third-down, pressure and Robert Griffin movement work, Friday the situations and the kicking game, and Saturday the opener walkthrough and the trip. Maurice Jones-Drew was cleared on Friday, September 12, after the week's last practice, so he played without a practice rep.

**Plan in force:** Talib and Verner outside, Bacarri Rambo and Trawick at safety and Jordan Poyer at nickel, with Daryl Smith relaying the call and the safeties echoing it ([the Week 2 plan](Regular-season%20Week%202.md)).  
**Game-day availability:** The seven inactives were the ones Stone set before the game: Nicks, Hoskins, Ball, Linsley, Edebali, Todd Davis and Gabriel. Jones-Drew dressed and started.

## 2. Pregame media

**Reporter:** Two defensive backs went on injured reserve Monday and you signed Alan Ball the same day. Walk us through the roster moves.

**Stone:** Mike went on injured reserve and Dwight went on with the designation to return, so he can practice in six weeks and play in eight if the doctors clear him. Both exams Monday said what Sunday night said. Alan took a physical and signed, and Adrian Phillips came up from the practice squad. That is Dave's part of it and I'll leave the terms to him.

**Reporter:** Who steps in for them, and what are you asking of Verner and Trawick this week?

**Stone:** Alterraun outside with Aqib, Brynden next to Bacarri, Jordan stays at nickel. Alterraun has started a lot of football games. The job this week was the communication, not the coverage: Daryl relays it, the safeties echo it, Alterraun declares his help. We ran that Monday and Wednesday before we ran anything else.

**Reporter:** Did you think about moving Poyer outside?

**Stone:** No. That is two changes to fix one injury.

**Reporter:** What's the status of Maurice Jones-Drew?

**Stone:** He was reassessed Monday and nothing changed, and his date was Friday. The trainers cleared him Friday. He did not practice this week.

## 3. The game

Two Jacksonville interceptions kept the game at 7-7 through the half, and it turned in the third quarter, when Jacksonville scored touchdowns off Washington turnovers on back-to-back possessions. Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions, each on a third down; the defense took the ball away three times and Jacksonville scored 17 points off them, while Washington scored only on its opening drive.

### First quarter

Washington took the opening kickoff and went eleven plays and 66 yards, Griffin finding Logan Paulsen for a 5-yard touchdown at 5:47. On third-and-1 at its own 49 Jacksonville threw the Dagger for Travis Kelce, and Bashaud Breeland intercepted it at 4:10. Late in the quarter, from the Jacksonville 16, the Power Pass to Davante Adams went 51 yards to the Washington 33.

### Second quarter

The drive the 51-yarder started went ten plays and 89 yards, finished by Jones-Drew's 11-yard Counter run on third-and-10 at 12:13 to tie it. Before the half Jacksonville ran from its 38 to the Washington 11 on Jones-Drew carries, then lost the chance when Duke Ihenacho intercepted the third-and-8 throw for Montell Owens at 1:18. Washington reached the Jacksonville 30 as the half ran out, 7-7.

### Third quarter

David Amerson intercepted the Spacing throw for Adams on third-and-11 at 11:19, and Washington gave the ball straight back: Paul Posluszny intercepted Griffin on third-and-5 at 9:18 and returned it 21 to the Washington 42. Two plays later C.J. Anderson ran 24 yards on Outside Zone Left for the go-ahead touchdown at 8:25. On Washington's next possession Roy Miller sacked Griffin, forced the ball out and recovered it at the Washington 16, and five plays later Cousins threw the Spacing call to Marcedes Lewis for a 1-yard touchdown at 5:10, 21-7.

### Fourth quarter

Washington did not get inside the Jacksonville 30 again. With 2:15 left Jeremy Mincey sacked Griffin, forced the fumble and recovered it at the Washington 14, and Josh Scobee's 30-yard field goal with 19 seconds left made it 24-7.

### The calls and decisions that shaped the game

The first interception came on a call the week's plan did not have for that down: on third-and-1 the plan named Power, Counter, Mesh and the access run, and the Dagger went in instead. Stone said so afterwards and put it on the sideline's procedure, not on the quarterback. The second came from the Washington 11 with 1:18 left in the half, on a throw for Owens that the play-by-play ties to no call on the sheet. Neither the play-by-play nor any staff review on record shows the coverage or the read on the three throws, and Stone said he would not divide them between himself and Cousins until he had seen them.

## 4. Postgame media

**Stone:** We won by seventeen on the road with four sacks and three takeaways and we ran the ball for 171. We also threw it to the other team three times, one of them from their 11, and gave up 127 return yards for the second week running. The three throws are mine before they are Kirk's. Go ahead.

**Reporter:** Was Kelce supposed to get the ball on third-and-1?

**Stone:** He was the target. Dagger on third-and-1 is not the sheet. The sheet has Power, Counter, Mesh and the access run there, and he got the gated call instead. That is the sideline, not the quarterback.

**Reporter:** What did you think of C.J.?

**Stone:** The 24-yard touchdown and the 12 to the 11 on the tying drive. Eight snaps, seven carries, 50 yards. He ran the outside zone the way Mike taught it in August.

## 5. Football review and next week's work

**Offense:** The run game carried the day, Counter and the Outside Zone off it producing both rushing touchdowns. The passing game gave the ball away three times on third downs, two of them, Stone said, on calls that should not have left the sideline in those situations.  
**Defense:** Four sacks, two of them strips the linemen recovered themselves, and three takeaways worth 17 points. After the opening drive Washington did not get inside the Jacksonville 30.  
**Special teams and game management:** Washington returned kicks for 127 yards, the second straight week over 100 against the coverage units.  
**What changes for the next game:** The sideline procedure that sent the Dagger on third-and-1, and the coverage lanes and kick placement behind the return yards, go to the staff's review the next day, the lanes and the placement graded separately. Both are reviews still to be held.

## 6. After-action report

### Injuries and availability changes

| Player | What was reported | Effect now | Next medical decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Julian Stanford | Upper extremity, minor; logged in the first quarter, not removed | Out, projected return September 19 | Reassessment September 15 |
| Lane Johnson | Lower extremity, minor; logged in the fourth quarter, not removed | Out, projected return September 17 | Reassessment September 15 |

### Players who stood out

Paul Posluszny's interception at the Jacksonville 42 turned the game, and Anderson scored two plays later. Julian Stanford had two sacks over Washington's left tackle. Roy Miller and Jeremy Mincey each forced and recovered a fumble on a sack. Maurice Jones-Drew ran 24 times for 112 yards and the tying touchdown in his first game back.

### Role or transaction consequences

No changes.

## 7. Final record and next game

**Record after game:** 2-0.  
**Standing / playoff result:** First in the AFC South at 2-0, with Indianapolis, Houston and Tennessee 1-1.  
**Next scheduled event:** Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts, Sunday, September 21, 1 p.m. ET, EverBank Field.
